proof_skeleton_nl: Define the shift-invariance predicate P(z) for integer shifts. Prove P(0), then use the unit-shift identity to prove that P is preserved by +1 and -1. Apply the two-sided induction principle on integers to conclude P(z) for all z, and finally unpack the definition of P and the notation f = F_n.

steps.derives: For every real x, f(x + 1) = f(x).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conclusion of L1.

steps.derives: P(0), i.e. for every real x, f(x + 0) = f(x).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of L2.

steps.derives: For every integer z, P(z) → P(z + 1).
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L3 with the unit-shift identity from A1; then generalize over z.

steps.derives: For every integer z, P(z) → P(z - 1).
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L4 with the unit-shift identity from A1; then generalize over z.
The predicate P satisfies the base case at 0 and is closed under both successor and predecessor, so the two-sided integer induction principle yields P(z) for all integers z.

steps.derives: For every real number x and every integer z, F_n(x + z) = F_n(x).
steps.trivial_justification: Unfold P and the notation f = F_n, then introduce arbitrary x and z to read A5 in the exact order of the target statement.
